title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Three Typical Cases of Invoice Crimes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Issues Three Typical Cases of Invoice Crimes

Currently, illegal and criminal activities involving invoices, such as illegally manufacturing invoices, selling illegally manufactured invoices, and issuing false invoices on behalf of others, remain highly rampant, exhibiting characteristics of networking, specialization, and industrialization. These activities not only directly trigger various types of tax-related illegal and criminal acts, causing substantial loss of tax revenue and fiscal income, but also facilitate other illegal and criminal acts such as corruption, bribery, money laundering, and fraud, seriously threatening the national economic and tax security, undermining the construction of a clean Party and government, and worsening the social security environment. To effectively curb the increasingly rampant trend of invoice-related illegal and criminal activities, the State Council decided at the end of 2008 to launch a nationwide special campaign against invoice crimes. Over more than a year since the campaign began, the People's Courts have adjudicated a number of invoice crime cases according to law and punished a large number of invoice criminals. However, affected by various factors, the current situation of invoice-related illegal and criminal activities remains very severe, with a persistently high incidence of cases and increasingly covert methods employed by criminals, making crackdowns more difficult. To severely crack down on invoice-related illegal and criminal activities according to law and maintain a high-pressure stance, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security recently jointly issued the "Notice on Severely Cracking Down on Invoice-Related Illegal and Criminal Activities," requiring continued in-depth promotion of the special campaign against invoice crimes, strengthening the crackdown on key areas and sources of invoice crimes, and ensuring that invoice crime cases are quickly tried, quickly adjudicated, and severely punished according to law. To support the special campaign, maintain tax administration order, deter lawless elements, and create a healthy, orderly, fair-competition, honest, and trustworthy market economic environment, the Supreme People's Court recently published three typical cases of invoice crimes:

1. Case of Defendant Liu Zhengyan and Two Others for Selling Illegally Manufactured Invoices

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing found through trial: In March 2009, defendant Liu Zhengyan purchased over 60,000 forged electronic air ticket itinerary receipts from others and, via the Internet, sold 300 copies to defendant Li Jiehua at a price of RMB 0.5 each. Li Jiehua then sold the electronic air ticket inquiry system, the electronic air ticket itinerary printing system, and the 300 electronic air ticket itinerary receipts obtained from Liu Zhengyan to defendant Nan Yuhu for RMB 1,500. On April 18, 2009, when Nan Yuhu was selling electronic air ticket itinerary receipts purchased from Li Jiehua to others, he was caught on the spot by public security personnel. Based on Nan Yuhu's confession, public security personnel arrested Li Jiehua and Liu Zhengyan respectively, and seized 65,324 forged electronic air ticket itinerary receipts from Liu Zhengyan's residence.

The Haidian District People's Court convicted the defendants of the crime of selling illegally manufactured invoices, sentencing Liu Zhengyan to five years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 100,000; sentencing Li Jiehua to two years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000; and sentencing Nan Yuhu to two years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000. After the judgment was pronounced, defendants including Liu Zhengyan refused to accept it and appealed. Upon trial, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rejected the appeals of Liu Zhengyan and others according to law and affirmed the original judgment.

2. Case of Defendant Zhang Li and Three Others for Illegally Manufacturing Invoices

The Jieshou City People's Court of Anhui Province found through trial: From February 2008 to May 2009, defendant Zhang Li rented civilian houses in places such as Jiazhuang Village, Yingnan Office, Jieshou City, and hired defendants Li Shukun, Dai Ling, and Liu Aili to illegally print fixed-amount service industry invoices for Nanjing City and Changzhou City in Jiangsu Province and Ningbo City in Zhejiang Province. On May 29, 2009, public security personnel searched the den where Zhang Li and others illegally manufactured invoices, seizing on the spot 13,500 finished fake invoices, 137,254 semi-finished fake invoices, and a batch of equipment for printing fake invoices.

The Jieshou City People's Court convicted the defendants of the crime of illegally manufacturing invoices, sentencing Zhang Li to five years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 100,000; sentencing Li Shukun to two years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 60,000; sentencing Dai Ling to one year's imprisonment, suspended for two years, and a fine of RMB 50,000; and sentencing Liu Aili to six months' imprisonment, suspended for one year, and a fine of RMB 50,000. After the judgment was pronounced, defendant Zhang Li refused to accept it and appealed. Upon trial, the Fuyang Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province rejected Zhang Li's appeal according to law and affirmed the original judgment.

3. Case of Defendant Cao Jiaqing and Ten Others for Illegally Manufacturing Invoices and Selling Illegally Manufactured Invoices

The Nanhui District People's Court of Shanghai found through trial: Defendant Cao Jiaqing had previously been sentenced to three years' imprisonment, suspended for four years, in 2006 for the crime of illegally manufacturing invoices. During the probation period, Cao Jiaqing gathered defendants Dong Yuehua, Cao Canfu, Cao Tiantian, and others to forge various types of invoices, including Shanghai commercial limited unified invoices and international air passenger transport invoices, in a rented house in Yuzhai Town, Linquan County, Fuyang City, Anhui Province, and sold the forged invoices to defendants Bai Xiaohong and others, profiting RMB 160,000. After purchasing forged invoices from Cao Jiaqing, Bai Xiaohong resold them to defendants Shi Lanhua, Ye Fuying, Shi Jianping, Li Xihua, Dong Liushou, Dong Shengyong, and others for profit. On April 19, 2008, public security personnel seized 819,652 unsold forged invoices of various types from the rented house where Bai Xiaohong lived, and seized a total of 190,698 unsold forged invoices of various types from the premises of defendants Shi Lanhua, Ye Fuying, Shi Jianping, Li Xihua, Dong Liushou, and Dong Shengyong.

The Nanhui District People's Court convicted defendants Cao Jiaqing, Dong Yuehua, Cao Canfu, and Cao Tiantian of the crimes of illegally manufacturing invoices and selling illegally manufactured invoices, sentencing them to imprisonment ranging from six years and nine months to two years and eight months, and imposing fines ranging from RMB 270,000 to RMB 100,000 respectively. The court convicted defendants Bai Xiaohong, Shi Lanhua, Ye Fuying, Shi Jianping, Li Xihua, Dong Liushou, and Dong Shengyong of the crime of selling illegally manufactured invoices, sentencing them to imprisonment ranging from four years and nine months to two years and one month, and imposing fines ranging from RMB 250,000 to RMB 50,000 respectively. After the judgment was pronounced, defendants including Cao Jiaqing refused to accept it and appealed. Upon trial, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rejected the appeals of Cao Jiaqing and others according to law and affirmed the original judgment.
